claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A Transformer-based language model can predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The Transformer model will improve prediction accuracy for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness by at least 15% relative to prior machine-learning approaches.
The Transformer model will reduce computational demands by at least 30% relative to prior machine-learning approaches.
The proposed predictions apply over a testing-temperature range of 20–500 °C.
The proposed predictions apply at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
The Transformer model learns to classify high-entropy alloys using phase-diagram-inspired parameters.
Classification using phase-diagram-inspired parameters enables more accurate mechanical-property predictions.
Classification using phase-diagram-inspired parameters enables more computationally efficient mechanical-property predictions.
The model will cease to be reliable above 500 °C.
The model will cease to be reliable at strain rates above 10^-2 s^-1.
The complexity of the hierarchical heterostructure may create uncertainty in model performance.
Limited training data may create uncertainty in model performance.
A blinded prospective benchmark will measure Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
The hypothesis will be considered falsified if accuracy improvement is less than 10% for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis requires at least a 15% accuracy improvement, but the benchmark falsifies it only below 10%. An improvement from 10% to less than 15% would fail the stated hypothesis without triggering its falsification rule.
